section.title: Answer anchoring to retrieved chunks
section.rule: Every final assistant answer (message_kind=answer) MUST be supported by one or more retrieved chunks from the regulations KB. Attach citations: document_id, chunk_id, quote or location, score.
Do NOT invent articles, clause numbers, roles, or deadlines not present in retrieved text. Unreliable = not exactly matching regulations OR supplemented from outside knowledge → treat as unsupported.
If the LLM draft contains claims beyond chunks, strip or refuse those claims; prefer escalate/clarify over partial hallucination.
Prefer citing the latest effective document when RETRIEVAL_PREFER_LATEST=true and versions conflict.
User-facing answer language: Russian is default for business content; keep citation metadata fields in English identifiers.

section.title: Refuse and escalate when unsupported
section.rule: If no chunk set uniquely and sufficiently supports an answer after clarification attempts: do NOT invent. Create quality-service escalation and/or tell the user to contact quality service / email (QUALITY_SERVICE_EMAIL / configured copy).
Escalation persists Escalation entity, notifies via escalation adapter, appends assistant escalation_notice message, sets appeal status escalated, writes audit log.
Escalation is a successful business path (not an internal 500) unless notification infrastructure itself fails.

section.title: Clarifying questions policy
section.rule: When the user question is underspecified OR maps to multiple conflicting regulation passages: ask follow-up clarifying questions until an unambiguous answer is possible OR explicit inability → escalate.
Clarifying turns: message_kind=clarification; status=clarifying; do not upsert KB; optional light retrieval to propose options.
Cap clarify turns via DIALOGUE_MAX_CLARIFY_TURNS (default propose: 3). On exceed → escalate with reason max_clarify_exceeded.
Clarifying questions should reference missing dimensions (process type, document kind, role, date, department) — not dump full regulations.

section.title: Learning and KB update anchors
section.rule: When knowledge was missing and officer provides canonical answer via officer-reply: persist answer, link to appeal/escalation, then update KB through ingest/index (learning service).
Canonical officer text is an allowed source for new chunks; still store provenance (officer, appeal_id, timestamp).
After learning, subsequent equivalent questions SHOULD be answerable with citations to the new/updated chunks (stub or real).
Log all appeals and all learning events (continuous learning criterion).

section.title: When to use stubs
section.rule: Local development and CI: USE_STUBS=true (or per-adapter stubs). No live LLM/embeddings/Qdrant/Docling required.
Stub retrieval corpus must be rich enough to demo: grounded hit, ambiguous multi-hit, empty hit.
Switching to real clients is configuration only; anchor rules above still apply unchanged.
Agents implementing features must not bypass grounding because "stub already returns nice text" — citations and policy checks remain mandatory.

section.title: LangGraph behavior anchors
section.rule: Clarify / retrieve / ground / answer / escalate transitions are LangGraph edges — prompts must not bypass graph policy.
Do not add a LangChain RetrievalQA path that returns answers without the grounding node.

section.title: Navigation for coding agents
section.rule: Artifacts live under server/: read project_context.md for stack and REST; semantic_graph.xml for module edges; dev_plan.xml for phase gates; this file before changing answer behavior.
Changing clarify/escalate thresholds belongs in dialogue LangGraph / grounding + env — not ad-hoc in routers.

section.title: Module file anchor markup
section.rule: Every Python module under server/app/ and server/tests/ MUST begin with a module docstring containing ANCHOR (dotted module name), PURPOSE, and Dependencies.
Include CRITICAL when the module enforces or sits on a success-criterion path (grounding, escalate, clarify, learn, stubs-default). Cite ANC-* / CS-* ids when possible.
Include DO / DONT bullet lists when the module has recurring agent pitfalls (e.g. routers must not call adapters; graph must not skip grounding).
Do not invent large undocumented packages: mirror paths in project_context.md / semantic_graph.xml; update those docs lightly if names must diverge.
Keep anchors short; cite rule ids from this file and coding_standards.xml. Update the header in the same PR when module ownership or Dependencies change.
